plan.estimand: Minimum sample size for binary prediction model development satisfying Riley et al. criteria for apparent-versus-adjusted R-squared precision and average outcome-risk margin of error
plan.hypothesis: Under expected shrinkage (0.95) with 10 candidate predictors and anticipated Cox-Snell R-squared 0.12 at prevalence 0.20, the sample size will be sufficient such that the absolute difference between apparent and adjusted Nagelkerke R-squared remains ≤0.05 and the average outcome-risk margin of error ≤0.05

parameters.name: Target average outcome-risk margin of error

assumptions: Prediction model is binary logistic regression with intercept only modification
Cox-Snell R-squared 0.12 reflects true model performance before shrinkage
Shrinkage factor 0.95 applied uniformly to apparent model performance
Nagelkerke R-squared scale used for absolute precision criterion (standard for binary models)
95% confidence level governs precision margin calculation
Default pmsampsize absolute precision criteria applied (max R-squared apparent-vs-adjusted difference)
Average outcome-risk margin of error 0.05 interpreted as ±0.05 on probability scale for predicted risk
missing_information: Confirmation that 'default absolute precision criteria' refers to pmsampsize package default thresholds for R-squared differences under binary development context
Clarification on whether average outcome-risk margin of error 0.05 should be verified post-hoc using achieved sample size via analytical formula or simulation
clarification_questions: The pmsampsize documentation specifies absolute precision criteria for R-squared; should the returned sample size be verified to satisfy both the shrinkage-based R-squared difference criterion AND the average outcome-risk margin of error independently?
For verification at the returned sample size, is a closed-form analytical calculation acceptable, or is simulation-based validation preferred?
scientific_notes: Riley et al. (2020, 2021) recommend sample-size calculations for prediction model development based on shrinkage and apparent-versus-adjusted R-squared differences rather than classical hypothesis testing power

pmsampsize version 1.1.3 implements binary logistic regression model development sample-size calculation via algorithm balancing overfitting penalty (shrinkage) and precision of predictor effect estimates

Cox-Snell R-squared is outcome-scale; conversion to Nagelkerke scale for precision criterion uses formula: R²_Nagelkerke = R²_Cox-Snell / (1 - exp(-R²_Cox-Snell / (2n) * XYsum)). Under anticipated parameters, this transformation affects reported precision margin

Average outcome-risk margin of error references predictive accuracy on probability scale; sensitivity analysis recommended if model is deployed in populations with substantially different outcome prevalence
